newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says Bhutto sacking will not affect ties.
newsitem.headline: Japan says Bhutto sacking will not affect ties.

text.p: Japan, Pakistan's main aid donor, said on Tuesday the sacking of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto would not affect relations between Tokyo and Islamabad.
"We do not think it is a situation that will affect relations with Japan," government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama told a regular news conference.
The Japanese embassy in Islamabad has informed Tokyo that the Pakistani capital remained peaceful, he said.
Japan has been Pakistan's biggest aid donor for several years, giving just more than half of the total foreign aid received by Pakistan.
In 1996, Japan extended $542 million in loans to Pakistan, mainly in yen grants for development projects, plus about $70 million in direct aid, Japanese officials said.
Pakistani President Farooq Leghari sacked Bhutto on Tuesday, accusing her government of widespread corruption and nepotism, and army units took over key installations in Islamabad.
